reason: The simulation is not yet executable end-to-end: main() is a no-op, initialization is incomplete, no run loop, network not used, no calibration or metrics, and no predictions are produced. There are critical issues that can be resolved in the next iteration to achieve a functional pipeline and baseline accuracy. We are only at iteration 0 of 3, so there is substantial room for improvement.

specific_areas: Implement main() to construct Simulation, run the daily loop, compute metrics, and output predictions for days 30-39.

Complete Simulation._initialize_entities_and_data: create all agents, initialize mask/info states for every agent, load/build multiplex network via NetworkBuilder, and instantiate all modules and environments.

Add Simulation.run() with correct module sequencing: policy -> market (deliveries and price) -> information diffusion -> network stats -> adoption decision (including deliveries and new orders) -> aggregation.
Load and use social_network.json; if unavailable, fall back to synthetic layers with clear logging.
Extend PersonAgent with required attributes (risk, sensitivities, compliance, fatigue) and map from agent_attributes.csv with reasonable defaults.
Compute evaluation metrics (RMSE/MAE/R2/peak timing error/final gap) against train_data for days 0-29.

Implement a simple bounded grid-search calibration over key parameters (beta_peer_*, beta_policy, fatigue_decay_rate, subsidy_pass_through, noise_temperature) with early stopping and basic validation checks.
Fix aggregation denominator to use total population size, not potentially sparse mask_state.
Persist outputs (daily adoption rate and price) and print predictions for days 30-39.
Add minimal error handling and reproducible seeding; log fallbacks clearly.

code_generation.adjustments: Implement missing core pieces: complete initialization, run loop, metrics, calibration stub, and outputs. Extend PersonAgent. Integrate NetworkBuilder. Ensure AdoptionAggregator uses population size. Maintain reproducible randomness (seed random and numpy).
